text: V-neck waistcoat — the V point sits 8 cm to 14 cm below the neck point (10 cm to 12 cm on a five-button front), each side angled 25° to 40° from vertical. A narrowing funnel that lengthens the torso, enlarges the chest and directs the eye to the neckwear.

U-neck waistcoat — the V intersection replaced by an arc of 6 cm to 15 cm radius (approaching the neck width on the deepest cuts). Softens the chest and reduces vertical aggression; broader, rounder, softer tailoring.

Notch-lapel waistcoat — a miniature jacket lapel 6 cm to 8 cm wide built with jacket gorge construction, the gorge set 5 cm to 8 cm below the shoulder and the roll line running through the top fastening.
Peak-lapel waistcoat — peak angle 100° to 115°, projecting 2 cm to 4 cm. Creates the shoulder-width illusion critical in formalwear; broader chest, more authority, stronger V shape.
Shawl-lapel waistcoat — one continuous spline with no notch and no gorge, its radius progression 3 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm blended from top to bottom. Flow, luxury, formality.
Notch lapel with collar band — a separate collar stand 1.0 cm to 1.8 cm high added to the lapel system and drafted like a jacket collar. Greater neck presence, richer architecture.
Back belt with buckle — a 2 cm to 3 cm strap centered on the waistline within 1 cm, giving 4 cm to 8 cm of adjustment; the back panel is drafted 2 cm to 4 cm larger to allow it.
